posts.title: I Followed a Pigeon for 47 Minutes. Here's What I Learned.
paragraphs: Yesterday I saw a pigeon walking with purpose. Not normal pigeon purpose, either. This pigeon looked like it had somewhere to be.
I followed it across three streets, past a bakery, and directly into a parking garage. Then it stopped. It looked at me.
I looked at it. Neither of us blinked.
Eventually it flew away. I have learned nothing.

posts.title: Scientists Still Don't Know Where All the Missing Tupperware Lids Go
paragraphs: We have sent robots to Mars. We have photographed black holes. We can make phones that translate languages in real time.
And yet nobody can explain the Tupperware drawer.
Every container has a lid when you buy it. Somehow, three months later, the lids have become a completely separate civilization.

posts.title: My Houseplant Has Started Looking at Me
paragraphs: I bought a small plant because someone told me plants are relaxing.
Nobody mentioned that plants have eyes.
Okay, technically this one doesn't have eyes. But every time I walk past it, I feel like it knows what I did.

posts.title: Local Man Discovers His Left Shoe Is Slightly More Powerful Than His Right Shoe
paragraphs: Greg noticed something unusual during his morning walk: his left shoe seemed to have considerably more confidence than the right one.
He tested the theory by walking to the refrigerator. The results were inconclusive.

posts.title: I Ranked Every Spoon in My Kitchen
paragraphs: There are seven spoons in my kitchen. After careful consideration, I have ranked them.
Spoon #4 came first because it "looked like it had experience."
Spoon #2 remains under investigation.

posts.title: Nobody Has Done Anything Interesting Today
paragraphs: After hours of searching for something worth reporting, our newsroom has reached an unfortunate conclusion.
Nothing happened.
We are reporting this anyway.

posts.title: What If Clouds Are Just Sky Potatoes?
paragraphs: For years, people have looked into the sky without asking the obvious question.
What if clouds are potatoes?
After staring at one for eleven seconds, our conclusion remains unchanged: probably potato.

posts.title: Five Ways to Look Busy While Doing Absolutely Nothing
paragraphs: Carry a notebook around without ever opening it.
Occasionally say "interesting" while staring at a wall.
Walk somewhere with confidence and then immediately forget why you went there.

posts.title: I Ate a Sandwich in the Exact Middle of the Day
paragraphs: At precisely an unspecified time, I consumed a sandwich.
The sandwich contained bread.
This is easily the most consequential lunch report I have ever written.

posts.title: My Calculator Has Too Many Buttons
paragraphs: I counted the buttons on my calculator.
Then I forgot the number.
I counted them again.
This process has changed nothing about my life.

posts.title: New Study Finds Hats Make You 73% More Hat-Like
paragraphs: The findings are difficult to argue with.
Participants wearing hats were noticeably more likely to be wearing hats.
Researchers described the results as "pretty obvious."

posts.title: Is a Hot Dog a Sandwich? We Refuse to Answer
paragraphs: After extensive consideration, our editorial team has decided that this question is somebody else's problem.
We have therefore written 900 words about refusing to write the answer.
You're welcome.

posts.title: Man Opens Refrigerator, Finds Exactly What He Expected
paragraphs: In a surprising development, a refrigerator contained the same objects it contained approximately ten minutes earlier.
"I was surprised," said Greg, despite having put the food there himself.

posts.title: Where Do Single Socks Go When They Escape the Dryer?
paragraphs: I put eight pairs of socks into the laundry. I retrieved seven pairs and one blue striped sock with no remaining purpose.
My prevailing theory is that missing socks pass through a temporary wormhole into another dimension where they lead fulfilling lives.
I respect their independence, but I still want my left sock back.

posts.title: I Stared at a Treadmill for 20 Minutes and Feel Exhausted
paragraphs: Gym experts tell us that consistency is key. Today I stood in front of a running treadmill for twenty full minutes.
Mental effort counts for at least 80% of cardio, according to zero legitimate doctors.
I rewarded myself with a smoothie and a nap.

posts.title: Why Does Microwave Minute Feel Twice as Long as Regular Minute?
paragraphs: Standard physics states time is linear and constant. Anyone reheating leftover soup knows this is a lie.
Sixty seconds on a microwave clock actually lasts approximately 4.5 standard human minutes.
Albert Einstein failed to account for waiting for hot cheese.

posts.title: I Stared at Stairs Until I Forgot How Walking Works
paragraphs: Stairs are just concrete shelves we step on to go upwards.
Once you realize this mid-step, your brain stops trusting your knees. I had to sit down on step 4 for ten minutes.
Elevators are clearly the superior lifestyle choice.

posts.title: Ducks Are suspiciously Calm in Cold Water
paragraphs: I visited the local pond yesterday while wearing three sweaters. The ducks were floating calmly in freezing water.
No shivering, no complaints, no hot cocoa in sight.
What are ducks hiding from us?

posts.title: I Drew a Circle and It Turned Out Slightly Oval
paragraphs: Attempting perfection is a human flaw. Today I tried drawing a flawless circle freehand.
The result resembled an egg that was mildly offended.
I am framing it as abstract minimalism.

posts.title: The Mystery of the Screws Left Over After Assembling Furniture
paragraphs: I built a bookshelf using clear pictorial instructions. The bookshelf stands straight and holds books.
Yet there are four silver screws and an Allen wrench lying on my rug.
Where did they belong? Does the bookshelf know? I am afraid to touch it.

posts.title: It Rained for Three Minutes Just to Make Me Look Foolish
paragraphs: I opened my umbrella, took three strides onto the sidewalk, and the sun immediately broke through the clouds.
The sky is mocking my weather app.
I carried the umbrella open for the rest of my walk to maintain authority.

posts.title: I Played Tic-Tac-Toe Against Myself and Lost
paragraphs: To test my tactical foresight, I played a friendly match of Tic-Tac-Toe against my left hand.
My right hand made a critical tactical blunder on turn three.
My left hand celebrated with a quiet fist bump.

posts.title: Who Is Pressing the Doorbell in My Dreams?
paragraphs: At 6:00 AM I woke up to a loud ding-dong chime ringing clearly in my mind.
I ran to the front door in my pajamas. Nobody was there except a squirrel looking nonchalant.
I am placing the squirrel on my suspect board.

posts.title: I Tried Toasting Bread Twice and Created Charcoal
paragraphs: Setting 3 was too soft. Setting 4 was acceptable. I wondered what Setting 6 would achieve.
My smoke alarm provided the definitive answer.
My kitchen smelled like a campfire for two days.

posts.title: An Elevator Jingle Has Been Stuck in My Head Since Tuesday
paragraphs: Three smooth synth notes played while descending to the ground floor. They have played continuously in my brain ever since.
I tried humming Beethoven to override it. Beethoven lost.
This elevator needs a record deal.

posts.title: Dandelions Are Just Weeds With Great Public Relations
paragraphs: If a plant grows uninvited in your lawn, it is a weed. But if you blow on it and make a wish, suddenly it is magic?
The branding team behind dandelions deserves a promotion.
My lawn is full of magical trespassers.

posts.title: Why Do We Wiggle Our Keys to Make Them Work Better?
paragraphs: My front door key refused to turn. I wiggled it gently, pulled it back 1 millimeter, and blew air into the keyhole.
It opened immediately.
Locks demand a ritual before granting passage.

posts.title: I Found a Nickel on the Sidewalk and Felt Rich
paragraphs: Five whole cents lying upside down near the curb. Free money from the universe.
I picked it up, wiped off the dirt, and felt like a successful treasure hunter.
My net worth increased by 0.002% instantly.

posts.title: I Read the Back of a Cereal Box and Was Moved to Tears
paragraphs: The maze on the back was complex yet achievable. The word search held profound truths.
Who wrote this masterpiece? Why haven't they won a Pulitzer Prize?
Breakfast literature is heavily underrated.

posts.title: Push vs Pull Doors: A Daily Human Struggle
paragraphs: I walked up to a glass door with a handleset. I pushed forcefully. Nothing moved.
A small sign said 'PULL'. I pulled. It opened effortlessly.
I pretended I was just testing the structural integrity of the frame.

posts.title: I Packed Three Extra Pairs of Pants Just in Case
paragraphs: I went on a two-day weekend trip to a town 30 miles away.
My luggage contained six shirts, five pairs of pants, and two raincoats. What did I anticipate? Spontaneous swamp survival?
I wore one pair of jeans the entire weekend.

posts.title: The Moon Was Out During the Day and It Felt Illegal
paragraphs: At 2:00 PM on a bright Thursday, I glanced up and saw the moon floating casually alongside the sun.
Who allowed this schedule overlap? Does the sun know?
Celestial management needs to check their calendar.

posts.title: If a Tree Falls in a Forest, Does It Make a Blog Post?
paragraphs: In conclusion, after writing 33 articles about spoons, pigeons, shoes, and cereal boxes, one ultimate truth emerges.
Everything is a potential blog post if you stare at it long enough.
Thank you for reading my extremely real thoughts.
